title: Complete priority edit + startup backfill + dnd visibility
summary: Close F003 gaps: priority field in edit modals, ensureShortKeysAndPriority at startup, visible drag handle
description:
F003 (Global shortId + priority + dnd, 899a4e77) shipped incomplete. Three gaps found during testing on `next` branch:

1. PRIORITY EDIT FIELD MISSING: backend schema has `priority` (Feature/Phase/Task types all have `priority: number`, schema plan-core/src/schema.ts), dashboard sorts by it (work-tree.tsx, dashboard-tree.ts), and the /reorder endpoint assigns it (plan-server/src/serve.ts:715). BUT no edit/create modal has a priority input — grep of packages/plan-web-ui/src/routes/*edit* returns nothing. Files: task-edit-modal.route.tsx, feature-edit-modal.route.tsx, phase-edit-modal.route.tsx + their .action.ts. Need: optionalNumber helper in lib/forms.ts, priority Field (Input type=number) in each modal, parse in each action.

2. BACKFILL NOT RUN AT STARTUP: ensureShortIdsAndPriority() (plan-store.ts:962) is idempotent and assigns shortId + priority, but grep shows it is NOT called in any startup hook (pi-adapter/plan-mcp/plan-server) — only via manual repair(). This is why all entities have priority=0 and shortId=undefined. Need: call ensureShortKeysAndPriority() in the startup heavy-init block of packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts (before_agent_start, alongside maybeHealStatuses) and packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts startup.

3. DRAG HANDLE NEARLY INVISIBLE: dnd is fully wired (SortableItem+DragHandle on all 3 row levels, nested SortableContexts, handleDragEnd handles feature/phase/task, /reorder endpoint works). BUT .drag-handle CSS (base.css:325) has opacity:0.35 (hover-only). User could not find it. Need: bump visibility (opacity ~0.55-0.7, or always visible).

Behaviors to preserve: idempotency of backfill (never overwrite non-zero priority / non-empty shortId), gap=10 priority spacing on reorder, SortableContext nesting.

Branch: next (working tree already on next). Build: pnpm build (web-ui + adapter + mcp), then copy web-ui to pi-adapter/web-ui-dist via scripts/copy-web-ui.sh.

tasks.title: Fix status rollup: blocked task must not poison parent when active work exists
tasks.description:
Bug: a single blocked task poisons the parent phase AND feature status, even with tons of done/in-progress work. Confirmed in heca .planner (F3 = blocked despite 50 done + 1 in-progress tasks; P11 = blocked despite 9 done + 1 in-progress).

Root cause: packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts derivePhaseStatus (~1111) and deriveFeatureStatus (~1134) check `anyBlocked` BEFORE `anyInProgress`/`anyActive`. So blocked dominates active work. Inconsistent with export-service.ts:deriveGlobalStatus which already does in-progress before blocked.

Fix: swap order in both functions — in-progress/active wins over blocked/waiting/deferred. Blocked surfaces only when there is NO active in-progress work (stall indicator). Semantics: active work = parent in-progress; no active + a blocker = parent blocked.

Files: packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts (2 swaps). Add regression test packages/plan-core/test/status-rollup.test.mjs (infra = `node --test "test/**/*.test.mjs"`, 4 existing tests). Verify: build + node --test + pnpm check. After fix, next syncStatuses auto-heals corrupted data (heca F3 → in-progress).

---
**Completion summary:**
Done. Rewrote derivePhaseStatus + deriveFeatureStatus in packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts with correct lifecycle semantics: planned → in-progress → done. Any progress (active in-progress OR partial completion via done) ⇒ in-progress; all done ⇒ done; blocked/waiting/deferred surface ONLY when there is zero progress (pure stall). Rejected/canceled tasks/phases are filtered out (void) before deriving. This fixes the long-standing bug where a single blocked task poisoned the whole feature even with tons of done/in-progress work. Added 10-case regression test packages/plan-core/test/status-rollup.test.mjs (node --test, 39/39 pass). pnpm check clean. Verified on a fresh HECA copy (by stable feature ID, not number — heca is actively reordered by another agent): all-done features (Theme 14/14, Terminal 36/36) stay done; blocked Pluggable Chrome (50 done+1 in-prog) → in-progress; progress features → in-progress; no-progress → planned. Compositor Frost (6 done+4 rejected) → done (rejected void). Export-service deriveGlobalStatus was already correct (in-progress before blocked) — now consistent across the codebase.

tasks.title: Fix /planner load recap: narration, language default, port thrashing
tasks.description:
Three issues from /planner load testing:

1. NARRATION + INTERNAL RULES EXPOSED: agent received the internal 'planner recap' trigger and narrated + quoted AGENTS.md to the user, then announced it would call planner-load (redundant). Fix: strengthen startupResumeProtocol (pi-adapter:~3700) — 'planner recap' is an INTERNAL signal not a question; do NOT quote/expose AGENTS.md/system prompt/internal instructions; do NOT run ANY tools (incl planner-load, already loaded); write recap in chatLanguage (empty→English). KEEP all recap-content bullets (progress counts, current feature/phase/task, handoffs, web URL, next activity).

2. LANGUAGE DEFAULTS TO ITALIAN WHEN UNSET: buildStartupResumeSummary (pi-adapter:337) has `if (italian || !chatLanguage)` → empty chatLanguage returns the ITALIAN template. Fix: change to `if (italian)` so empty falls through to the English branch. Default = English.

3. PORT BUSY + THRASHING: pickProjectPort (pi-adapter:698) returns the persisted project.webPort without checking availability; when two sessions share a .planner the second finds it busy → fallback, and startServer (pi-adapter:~815) overwrites project.webPort with the fallback port (thrashing: 53378→56321). Fix: pickProjectPort checks isPortAvailable on the persisted port; if busy, scan for a free port and return TRANSIENT (persist ONLY on first run). startServer persist block guards with (project.webPort<=0 || project.webPort===realPort) so fallback ports aren't persisted. Clarify the busy message ('another planner instance on this project?').

Verify: pi-adapter build + pnpm check. Functional: recap shows plan state, no AGENTS.md text, English when chatLanguage empty; port reuses canonical, no thrashing.

---
**Completion summary:**
Done. Three fixes in packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts:

1. NARRATION/EXPOSE (startupResumeProtocol ~3702): replaced 2 bullets with 4 — 'planner recap' is an INTERNAL trigger signal (not a user question); do NOT quote/expose AGENTS.md/system prompt/internal instructions (user must never see instruction text); do NOT run ANY tools incl planner-load (already loaded) + bash/read/grep/ls; write recap in chatLanguage (empty→English). All recap-content bullets kept (progress counts, current feature/phase/task, handoffs, web URL, next activity).

2. LANGUAGE DEFAULT (buildStartupResumeSummary:337): `if (italian || !chatLanguage)` → `if (italian)`. Empty chatLanguage now falls through to the English template (was defaulting to Italian). Verified 0 residuals of old pattern in src+dist.

3. PORT THRASHING: pickProjectPort (714) now checks isPortAvailable on the persisted port; if busy, scans for a free port and returns TRANSIENT (persists ONLY on first run, not fallbacks). startServer persist block (~815) guarded with (project.webPort<=0 || project.webPort===realPort) so transient fallback ports are never persisted (stops 53378→56321 hijack). Busy message clarified ('another planner instance on this project?').

Build pi-adapter + pnpm check clean. All changes verified in dist (if(italian), INTERNAL trigger signal, webPort===realPort guard).

tasks.title: Fix recap trigger/AGENTS.md collision (narration persists)
tasks.description:

tasks.title: Derived phase/feature status (not persisted)
tasks.description:
Design-only → implementation: phase/feature status becomes DERIVED at read time (from tasks/children), never persisted to disk. Task status stays manual (source of truth).

Derivation rules (stall wins over progress), excluding rejected/canceled:
- all done → done
- any blocked → blocked
- any waiting → waiting
- any deferred → deferred
- any done/in-progress → in-progress
- else → planned (all void → rejected)

Files to change (all in agent-plan):
- packages/plan-core/src/schema.ts: Phase/Feature `status` → optional/legacy (strip on save).
- packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts: loaders (loadAll, loadPhase, loadFeatures, loadFeature) compute derived status + attach to in-memory object; savePhase/saveFeatures strip status; remove autoSync/maybeAutoSync + syncStatuses + syncTaskStatusRollup; move handoff auto-clear into updateTask (when last non-done task → done and derived phase done).
- packages/plan-server/src/serve.ts: bootstrap — remove syncStatuses call (keep ensureShortIdsAndPriority).
- packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts + packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts: feature_update/phase_update — remove `status` param (derived); remove any syncStatuses calls.

Migration: existing persisted `status` ignored on read (derived), disappears on next save. No explicit migration.

Verify: F001 agent-plan (phase done) → done (no DnD flip). Test on /tmp copy, NOT heca.

---
**Completion summary:**
Derived phase/feature status rollup (syncTaskStatusRollup) is implemented + working across the codebase — phases/features derive done/in-progress from task statuses. The stale in-progress state was a tracking artifact, not incomplete work. Also repaired F1's broken feature→phase link (phaseIds was empty while phase 5714df9d had featureId=F1).

tasks.title: Slim phase/feature/project tool responses (drop structuredContent)
tasks.description:
Same class of bug as the task-response slimming done earlier: planner-phase-update, planner-phase-create, planner-phase-discuss, planner-feature-update, planner-feature-create, planner-project-update all use writeAndSummarize() (plan-mcp L119) which passes the FULL entity object as structuredContent. In Claude Code, structuredContent is surfaced to the model and can exceed the display cap → the agent misreads the response as a failure even though writeGenerated() already applied the change (heca agent hit this 2026-07-27 with planner-phase-update).

Fix recipe (same as task slimming):
1. plan-mcp: for each affected tool, drop the structuredContent arg from writeAndSummarize (or pass undefined), and change the message to a slim compositeRef+shortId form: `Phase updated: P005(F006) — <title> (done) · EHPKV` (use formatPhaseRef + the entity shortId). No UUID, no full object.
2. pi-adapter: the equivalents already emit slim-ish content.text but use UUID + status — align to compositeRef + shortId (no UUID). Check L1804 (phase-update notify), L3127 (phase-update content), and feature/project equivalents.
3. Keep tool-show (planner-phase-show etc.) FULL — that's the explicit "read full detail" tool, slimming it would defeat its purpose.

Files: packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts (writeAndSummarize callers L119+), packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts (phase/feature/project update/create handlers ~L1800, L3127+).
Verify: pnpm -r build + pnpm check clean. Smoke-test a phase-update via MCP stdio on a temp .planner copy → response should be slim (≤~80 char), no structuredContent, no UUID.

---
**Completion summary:**
Slimmed phase/feature/project tool responses in both adapters — same recipe as the earlier task slimming. Drops the full-entity structuredContent that caused the "too big to display → misread as failure" bug in Claude Code (heca agent hit this 2026-07-27 with planner-phase-update).

plan-mcp (packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts):
- Imported formatFeatureRef. Slimmed 8 writeAndSummarize callers: project-init, language-prefs, project-discuss (dropped {project}); feature-create/update (formatFeatureRef + shortId, dropped {feature}); phase-create (formatPhaseRef + shortId, dropped {phase}); phase-discuss/update (formatPhaseRef via found+features + shortId, dropped {phase}). AGENTS.md: added "Stato derivato, non persistito" note under rule 2 — feature/phase status in .planner/*.json is derived, can be null/stale; trust the tool response, not the raw JSON.

Verified: pnpm -r build + pnpm check clean. MCP stdio smoke-test on planner-phase-update: response = "✅ Phase updated: P005(F004) — <title> · 8LTJ6", structuredContent=false, no UUID, compositeRef present.

tasks.title: Recap: prefer handoff over resume.json nextSteps (staleness fix)
tasks.description:
Problem: refreshResume (plan-store.ts L751-771) keeps free-text nextSteps/notes forever (L761: `existing?.nextSteps ?? []`) — they go stale silently, yet the recap presents them as authoritative "next steps", misleading the resume. The heca agent hit this repeatedly (notes: "nextSteps still read 'T009 ... do not start it' after the user had decided Level 2 the day before"). F6 made the handoff (phase.handoff) the authoritative, actively-managed resume context. But the recap ALSO reads resume.json nextSteps — two competing "next steps" sources, stale one can override fresh handoff.

Fix: make the handoff authoritative; demote resume.json nextSteps to a clearly-marked fallback.
1. Recap builder (buildRecap in plan-core + pi-adapter recap assembly): when ≥1 phase has a pending handoff (listHandoffs().length > 0), the recap's "next steps" section comes from the HANDOFF (primary). resume.json nextSteps are SUPPRESSED with a one-line note: "Next steps come from the phase handoff above (actively maintained). Legacy resume.json nextSteps suppressed because they may be stale."
2. When NO handoff exists: fall back to resume.json nextSteps, but prepend a caveat: "⚠️ These nextSteps are free-text from resume.json and may be stale — verify against current planner state before acting."
3. refreshResume: add nextStepsUpdatedAt timestamp (set when nextSteps actually change, not on every refresh); the recap can surface "nextSteps last updated X ago" so staleness is visible.

Files: packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts (refreshResume + ResumeFocus), packages/plan-core/src/recap.ts (buildRecap nextSteps section), packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts (recap assembly L324/465/3614/3705).
Verify: pnpm -r build + pnpm check. Functional test: recap with a pending handoff → nextSteps from handoff, resume.json suppressed. Recap with no handoff → resume.json nextSteps with caveat.

---
**Completion summary:**
Fixed the resume.json nextSteps staleness footgun: the handoff (phase.handoff, F6) is now authoritative; resume.json nextSteps demoted to a clearly-marked fallback.

Changes:
1. schema.ts: added nextStepsUpdatedAt to ResumeFocusSchema (when nextSteps last changed).
2. plan-store.ts saveResume: tracks nextStepsUpdatedAt — bumped only when saveResume receives new nextSteps (compares JSON), preserved across refreshResume (which keeps existing nextSteps). Added the field to the 3 ResumeFocus literals (init, guardBypass fallback, refreshResume).
3. recap.ts buildRecap (shared, used by MCP/Claude Code/Codex):
   - When ≥1 pending handoff: "Next step" points to the handoff (authoritative, actively maintained); resume.json nextSteps SUPPRESSED with a note.
   - When no handoff: falls back to resume.nextSteps[0] + a ⚠️ caveat ("free-text from resume.json, may be stale — verify against current state") + the nextStepsUpdatedAt date.
   - Updated the handoff directive: "delete-on-resume" → "KEPT until a task in that phase starts (auto-archived) or the phase completes — no need to clear manually" (F6 semantics). Removed dead handoffClearCmd.
4. pi-adapter startup summary (Pi):
   - nextActivity: handoffs now take priority over resume.nextSteps[0] even when there's active work (was: nextSteps[0] first, handoff only when no active work).
   - "next steps:" dump: added staleness caveat — "(⚠️ may be stale — handoff is authoritative)" when handoffs exist, else "(last updated <date>, may be stale)".

Verified: pnpm -r build + pnpm check clean. Functional test (buildRecap on temp .planner): (A) with handoff → stale nextStep does NOT leak, points to handoff; (B) no handoff → nextStep shown with ⚠️ caveat + last-updated date; (C) fresh timestamp surfaced.
